name: IBPS Clerk (CSA)
tagline: Customer Service Associate (clerical cadre) in public sector banks, recruited state-wise

overview.about: IBPS conducts the Common Recruitment Process for Customer Service Associates (clerical cadre) in participating public sector banks. Selection is through an online Prelims and Mains followed by a language proficiency test; there is no interview, so Mains marks decide the final merit.
eligibility: Graduation in any discipline by the closing date of registration
Age 20–28 years on the date fixed in the notification; relaxation: SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC-NCL 3 yrs, PwBD 10 yrs
Proficiency in the official language of the state/UT applied for (read, write, speak)
Computer literacy (certificate/diploma or computer subject in school/college)

pattern.note: Revised 2025 pattern; confirm sectional timings in the current notification

chapters.title: Strategy, state-wise cut-offs & the revised Mains

cards.title: Mains-only merit
cards.body: Prelims only qualifies you. Final provisional allotment is based on **Mains marks out of 200**, state-wise and category-wise, after you clear the language test. There is no interview.

cards.title: Revised Mains (2025)
cards.body: Questions fell from **190 to 155** and time from **160 to 120 minutes**, but total marks stay **200**. Reasoning now carries **60 marks for 40 Q** (1.5 marks each), so every reasoning question counts more.

cards.title: Marks per question
cards.body: Reasoning 1.5, Quant ≈1.43, GA 1.25 and English 1.0 marks per question. When stuck, move to the section with the higher value per question first — but only if sectional timing allows it in your notification.

cards.title: Prelims accuracy
cards.body: Clerk Prelims cut-offs are high and close. Accuracy of **90%+** on attempted questions matters more than attempting everything. Avoid 50-50 guesses in the last minute of a section.

cards.title: State choice
cards.body: Vacancies are state-wise. You must know the official language of the state you apply for. Check past state-wise cut-offs on the IBPS site before choosing.

cards.q: In the revised IBPS Clerk Mains, Reasoning has 40 questions for 60 marks. Marks per question?
IBPS Clerk final allotment is based on:
options: Mains only (after qualifying the language test)
cards.explain: There is no interview; Mains marks decide the merit.

notes.p: IBPS Clerk recruits **Customer Service Associates (CSAs)** for participating public sector banks. There is a **Prelims**, a **Mains** and a **language proficiency test**. There is **no interview**. Prelims only qualifies you; the **provisional allotment is based on Mains marks (out of 200)**, **state-wise and category-wise**.
points: Prelims: English, Numerical Ability, Reasoning; sectional timers.
Mains: decides merit.
Language proficiency test: qualifying, conducted by the allotted bank.
Negative marking: ¼ of the question's marks.

notes.h: The revised Mains (2025) and marks per question
notes.p:
In the revised pattern, Mains fell from **190 to 155 questions** and from **160 to 120 minutes**, while total marks stayed **200**. Section-wise: **Reasoning 40 Q for 60 marks**, **Quant 35 Q for 50 marks**, **General/Financial Awareness 40 Q for 50 marks**, **English 40 Q for 40 marks** (check the current notification for timings and any changes).

**Worked example: marks per question**
Reasoning: 60 ÷ 40 = **1.5**.
Quant: 50 ÷ 35 ≈ **1.43**.
GA: 50 ÷ 40 = **1.25**.
English: 40 ÷ 40 = **1.0**.
Check totals: 40 + 35 + 40 + 40 = 155 questions; 60 + 50 + 50 + 40 = 200 marks ✓.
A wrong Reasoning answer costs 1.5 × ¼ = **0.375** marks, so careless attempts there hurt the most.
Clerk Prelims cut-offs are high and closely bunched, so small errors decide who qualifies.
points: Target **90%+ accuracy** on attempted questions.
Do quick topics first: simplification, series, inequality, syllogism, coding.
Leave a puzzle if it is not opening up within 4 minutes.
Avoid 50-50 guesses in the last minute of a section.

notes.p: Vacancies are announced **state-wise**. You must know the **official language of the state** you apply for. Check past state-wise cut-offs on the IBPS website, but let language ability decide your choice. After Mains, candidates are provisionally allotted to banks based on merit, state, category and preferences.

points: Treating Reasoning like a 1-mark section; it carries 1.5 marks per question.
Neglecting GA because Prelims has none.
Choosing a state for its cut-off, not its language.
Using an old 190-question mock pattern for practice.

notes.p:
Each Reasoning question carries 1.5 marks; a wrong answer costs 1.5 × ¼ = 0.375.
**Candidate A:** attempts 30, gets 27 right and 3 wrong → 27 × 1.5 − 3 × 0.375 = 40.5 − 1.125 = **39.375**.
**Candidate B:** attempts 34 (four extra guesses), gets 28 right and 6 wrong → 28 × 1.5 − 6 × 0.375 = 42 − 2.25 = **39.75**.
Four extra risky attempts added only 0.375 marks and took time that could have gone to sure questions elsewhere. Extra attempts help only when you can eliminate options confidently.

points: No interview; Mains decides merit.
Revised Mains: 155 Q, 120 min, 200 marks.
Reasoning 1.5, Quant ≈1.43, GA 1.25, English 1.0 marks per question.
Prelims accuracy 90%+.
State-wise selection; know the state language.
Language test is qualifying.

cards.title: What it tests
cards.body: Candidates must **read, write, speak and understand** the official language of the state/UT applied for. The test is **qualifying**, conducted by the participating bank after provisional allotment.

cards.title: Why banks insist
cards.body: CSAs work at the counter and with walk-in customers, many of whom prefer the local language. Communicating clearly is part of the job, not an extra.

cards.title: Preparation
cards.body: Practise reading notices, simple forms and a short paragraph aloud; write 5–6 sentences about yourself; hold a short conversation about opening an account or a loan enquiry.

cards.title: Allotment flow
cards.body: Mains result → provisional allotment to a bank based on merit, state and preference → document verification and language test by the bank → appointment. Failing the language test means losing the allotment.

cards.title: Keep proof ready
cards.body: If you studied the language in school, keep certificates/mark sheets ready; banks may consider them during verification as per the notification's rules.

cards.q: The language proficiency test for IBPS Clerk is:
cards.explain: It is qualifying; it does not add marks to the merit.

cards.q: Who usually conducts the language test?
cards.explain: The participating bank conducts it after provisional allotment.

notes.h: What the language proficiency test checks
notes.p: Candidates must be able to **read, write, speak and understand** the **official language of the state/UT** they applied for. The test is **qualifying** and is conducted by the **participating bank** after provisional allotment. It adds no marks, but failing it means losing the allotment.

CSAs work at the counter and with walk-in customers. Many customers, especially in semi-urban and rural branches, prefer the local language for explaining problems, filling forms or asking about loans. Clear communication prevents errors, builds trust and is part of the job, not an extra skill. For example, a farmer asking about a crop loan, or an elderly pensioner whose passbook entry looks wrong, will explain the problem fully only if the officer understands them easily.

notes.h: The allotment flow, step by step
notes.p: Understanding the order of events helps you prepare at the right time.
points: Step 1: Mains result and state-wise merit list.
Step 2: provisional allotment to a participating bank based on merit, state, category and preferences.
Step 3: the bank conducts **document verification** and the **language test**.
Step 4: appointment after both are cleared (and medical fitness, as applicable).
Keep school certificates/mark sheets showing the language; the bank may consider them as per the notification's rules.

notes.h: Preparation plan with a worked practice task
notes.p:
Practise for 20–30 minutes a day once Mains is over.

**Daily routine:** read a short local-language news item aloud (5 min); write 5–6 sentences about yourself or a banking topic (10 min); hold a short role-play conversation (10 min).

**Worked practice task:** Role-play a loan enquiry.
Customer: asks about a two-wheeler loan.
You (in the local language): greet, ask about income proof and identity documents, explain that the bank will check eligibility, mention that the EMI depends on the loan amount, rate and tenure, and offer the application form.
Repeat with deposits, ATM card blocking and passbook updates until the vocabulary feels natural.

points: Waiting until allotment to start practising.
Practising only speaking, not reading and writing.
Not carrying school documents that show the language.
Choosing a state whose language you cannot use comfortably.

notes.p: The test is a practical check of whether you can serve customers, not a literature exam. Evaluators usually look for four things.
points: **Reading:** can you read a notice or form aloud without long pauses?
**Writing:** can you write simple, correct sentences in the script of the language?
**Speaking:** can you explain a banking process clearly and politely?
**Understanding:** can you follow a customer's question and respond sensibly?
Simple vocabulary used confidently is better than complex words used wrongly.
Read, write, speak, understand the state's official language.
Qualifying; conducted by the allotted bank.
Order: Mains → allotment → document verification + language test → appointment.
Practise banking conversations daily.
Keep language certificates ready.
